solution: Under 'India's Security System' the chapter says: "The President of India is the supreme commander of the defence forces. The defence forces cannot take any decisions about war or peace without the consent of the President, because the latter represents the civil power." The Prime Minister and Defence Minister are the tempting rivals — the chapter notes the Ministry of Defence controls the three forces — but only the President is named as supreme commander, and it is also the President who appoints the three service chiefs.

Under 'Paramilitary Forces' the chapter says: "The Coast Guard has been created to protect India's oceanic borders. The Coast Guard carries out tasks like protecting the fishing occupation within Indian maritime borders, preventing smuggling along sea routes, etc." Note the chapter also says "the Navy protects the coastline", but the Navy is not among the four options; of those offered, the Army is explicitly assigned the geographical land boundaries, the BSF the land border, and the RAF riot/blast response — so Coast Guard is the only coastline body listed.

The chapter states almost verbatim: "The National Cadet Corps (NCC) has been established with the purpose of instilling among students the love of discipline and military training. Boy and girl students from schools and colleges can join the NCC." The BSF, CRPF and RAF are each given quite different tasks in the same section (border patrolling, aiding State law and order, and rapid response to blasts or riots respectively) and none of them involves students.
